task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about permanent electricity connections planned for the public market in Slateford. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Slateford Council approved a $132,000 installation budget for permanent electrical supply points at the town's outdoor market.
The plan provides 14 shared pedestals with two separately booked outlets each, making 28 bookable outlets.
The market currently has 52 registered stallholders, though not all trade on every market day or need electricity.
Stallholders who need power currently use a mixture of permitted generators and arrangements with nearby premises.
Construction is planned between the winter market season and the March 2027 reopening, subject to final contractor scheduling.
The project budget covers installation and inspection; electricity charges and ongoing maintenance will remain operating expenses.
The council has not announced a charge for booking an outlet or a formula for allocating electricity costs among users.
Market manager Elva Rane said, "Power will become something we book and maintain together, rather than something each stall improvises separately."
The outlet plan limits the equipment load at each pedestal, and approval for one appliance does not imply approval for every appliance a trader owns.
Licensed contractors will install and inspect the equipment before it becomes available for use.
The market will assign powered positions through a published booking process rather than let traders claim a socket by arriving first.
Food trader Neri Vale said, "A reliable socket would help, but the running charge matters as much as the installation announcement."
Traders who sell products without powered equipment asked that the eventual fee system identify which costs are shared by the whole market.
The council will consult stallholders on operating charges before adopting the next market fee schedule.
The plan leaves pedestrian access lanes clear and places supply points along existing service edges rather than in the middle of the public aisle.
Some stall locations will change to match the supply layout, but the final assignment map has not been issued.
The council has not supplied measurements of the current market's generator emissions or predicted a numerical reduction in noise.
The project does not include charging facilities for customers' vehicles or unrestricted public use of the market outlets.
The market occupies a square paved in alternating stone bands that have long been used as informal stall-position guides.
The market office will hold equipment-registration sessions before assigning powered spaces.
Existing generator permissions remain in effect until replacement arrangements are announced; the installation vote itself does not revoke them.
The council has not approved an increase in the market's total number of stalls as part of this project.

forbidden_additions: Free power, an announced tariff or an outlet guaranteed for every registered stall.
Immediate cancellation of generator permissions or public vehicle charging.
Measured emissions benefits or a final stall-assignment map.
preserve: Capital installation distinguished from unresolved operating charges and allocation.
Different needs of powered and unpowered traders.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
